title: Control Plane Ops: deep-dive gaps and ops playlist
body:
Attendees: Priya, Mateo, Arielle, Samir, Elena

Purpose: quick weekly sync with a focused deep-dive into two recurring pain areas we saw in the last 72h: auth token expiries that bubbled into a route-fallback storm, and quota fragmentation causing uneven throttles across customers. Goal: surface concrete mitigation steps we can ship this sprint and capture temporary runbook changes for on-call.

Notes:
- Incident sketch (May 17): upstream auth refresh service (auth-refresh-svc) returned sporadic 502s ~ 03:12–03:47 UTC. Impact: ~1.8% of production requests retried into fallback tier, which in turn saturated lower-cost routing pool and increased tail latency for non-affected customers.
- Root cause hypothesis: auth-refresh-svc had a degraded connection pool to KMS during a noisy GC on the host; retry storm due to our current client backoff being too aggressive and no jitter.
- Side effects observed: quota accounting continued to charge tokens for retried attempts because counting happens pre-auth success; this caused several customers to cross quota thresholds unexpectedly.

What we measured:
- Spike timeline: auth error rate peaked at 03:19 UTC.
- Fallthrough routing rate rose from baseline 0.2% to 1.9% during window.
- Median token billing delta for affected accounts +0.6% for period (ballpark).

Immediate mitigations (short horizon, ship in 24–72h):
1) Adjust auth client backoff: increase initial backoff to 150ms, add full jitter, cap retries to 2. (Owner: Mateo, ETA: 48h)
2) Change billing checkpoint: move quota billing to post-auth-success for retries under 1s window to avoid double-charging transient failures. This will be an opt-in toggle behind feature flag for beta accounts. (Owner: Priya, ETA: 72h)
3) Temporary routing throttle: when fallthrough rate > 1% for >5m, apply soft cap to fallback pool to preserve latency SLOs for critical customers. Implemented as an emergency policy in the control plane. (Owner: Samir, ETA: 24h for runbook, 72h for policy)

Longer-term work (next milestone / next two sprints):
- Quota reconciliation engine: create an eventual-consistency reconciliation job that re-evaluates billing records and emits corrective credits for detected double-charges. Prototype scheduled in sprint; initial POC will cover accounts with >0.3% unexplained billing drift. (Owner: Elena, ETA: 2 sprints)
- Improve KMS client observability: instrument per-request KMS latencies and attach a heatmap to the auth-refresh dashboards so we can correlate GC/host-level events with KMS anomalies. (Owner: Arielle, ETA: 3 sprints)
- Revisit routing fallback strategy: define customer-classed fallback priorities (tiered fallthrough). Customers with SLAs should be pinned away from low-cost fallbacks during perturbations. Requires console + control-plane rollout. (Owner: Platform PM + Priya, ETA: roadmap 6–8 weeks)

Decisions made in this meeting:
- Do the backoff/jitter change now; no risk to compatibility, expected to reduce retry amplification.
- Billing checkpoint shift will be feature-flagged and gated; we will run a closed beta with three pilot accounts.
- Add emergency soft-cap to fallback routing to protect latency SLOs; this becomes part of the on-call triage checklist.

Runbook / playbook additions (quick drafts):
- When auth-refresh-svc 5xx > 0.5% for 10m:
  * Page SRE rotation.
  * Flip fallback soft-cap to 50% of normal throughput for non-SLA customers.
  * Open ephemeral ticket to KMS team with correlation window + example request ids.
  * If billing drift > 0.4% in a customer cohort, tag for reconciliation batch.

Open questions / risks:
- Moving billing post-auth will complicate edge-cases for streaming/tokenized endpoints where tokens accrue while the client negotiates streaming; need to vet with SDK teams.
- Soft-cap decision could create denial-of-service-like behavior for low-tier customers during prolonged KMS outages; need clear comms and automated credits.
- Can we add mutual TLS verification to auth-refresh-svc hosts to reduce KMS transient errors? Security impact analysis needed.

Action items (owners + next steps):
- Mateo: implement and deploy auth-client backoff + jitter; create unit tests and add to chaos bench. (PR due: 2026-05-21)
- Priya: design feature flag plan for billing checkpoint shift; identify 3 pilot accounts and draft comms. (Plan due: 2026-05-22)
- Samir: author emergency routing soft-cap runbook and add play to on-call binder. (Runbook draft: 2026-05-20)
- Elena: start quota-reconciliation POC; gather sample accounts and expected correction budgets. (POC kick: 2026-05-25)
- Arielle: add KMS request histograms to the auth dashboard and create alert for median > 200ms for 10m. (Dashboard PR: 2026-05-28)

Small experiments to run in parallel:
- Canary test backoff change on dedicated-internal cluster first; observe retry amplification and fallthrough.
- Synthetic KMS latency inject on staging to validate new dashboard alerts.
- Billing toggle staged for server-side only; run with server logs to verify no streaming regressions.

Notes to self / drafting ideas:
- Consider a short-lived "retry-silencer" flag: if a request has visible KMS error but succeeds on subsequent attempt within 200ms, mark it non-billable. Could be abused, needs strict conditions.
- Potential metric: "retries-per-successful-auth" as a first-class SLI.

Quick status updates from owners (round-robin):
- Mateo: already have PR sketch, need test harness; expects low risk.
- Priya: booking pilot accounts with CS and legal for billing test.
- Samir: added runbook skeleton in the shared on-call doc; wants review.
- Elena: will reuse existing reconciliation infra from billing-team prototypes.
- Arielle: will add KMS histograms as separate dashboard tile to avoid clutter.

Closing notes:
- Next check-in scheduled Tue 2026-05-25 for progress on short-horizon items and first canary outcomes.
- If auth-refresh shows any 5xx spike before then, owners should convene ad-hoc (Slack #controlplane-ops) rather than wait for scheduled sync.

Appendix: quick links and example logs to attach (will paste in follow-up comment):
- sample-request-ids: r-20260517-3k7h, r-20260517-3k8m
- quick grep pattern for logs: "auth-refresh-svc.*error.*kms"

Unresolved: assign a single owner for communications to CS/legal for billing credits (Priya to coordinate but needs sign-off).

End of notes.
